> Step right into Sector C with the Lambda Terminal—a custom-built, retro-futuristic macro and MIDI keypad heavily inspired by the iconic Black Mesa aesthetic. Built on a sleek black PCB with punchy orange silkscreen details and glowing ENIG gold exposed copper for the touch zones (featuring cool honeycomb and zigzag patterns), this board looks like it was smuggled straight out of a classified research facility. Powered by an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, it’s not just a gorgeous display piece: it packs a crisp OLED screen, a rotary encoder for smooth navigation, tactile push buttons, a buzzer for retro audio feedback, and custom capacitive touch areas that pick up the electrical field of your fingers. Whether you're dropping custom beats, executing complex shortcuts, or just feeling like a senior scientist running the facility, this terminal blends top-tier sci-fi style with serious hardware power.

### Today's Progress: Schematic & Design Finalized

Today was all about wrapping up the schematic and laying down the groundwork for the physical layout. I officially finished the wiring schematic for the console!

After playing around with a few concepts, I decided to give the physical design a fun thematic twist: **the controller layout is styled after the iconic *Half-Life* universe, featuring the unmistakable Lambda symbol as a core design element.**

Bringing this together wasn't overly complicated, but like any electronics project, it came with a few minor roadblocks. I ran into a couple of small schematic errors along the way, but they were relatively easy to debug and clear up.

### Next Steps
* **Tomorrow:** Start the PCB layout and routing phase based on today's finalized schematic.
